display_name: Dispatch a work turn into a managed session
description: Fleet session-management, D2-window rider (rotation-boundary ruling 2026-08-04), with EFFECT VERIFICATION added 2026-08-19 (public issue #9, GAU-09's sibling fix). Sends an arbitrary work turn (the 'text' argument) over the resolved host driver's driver channel to the running process behind agent_instance_id, then -- where that driver can read its target back -- polls for a positive signature that the text left the composer without ever being observed sitting there stranded, before answering. The bootstrap dispatch verb: spawn_session boots a worker with no first turn, so drive_session is how the steward hands a spawned worker its brief and every later follow-up turn. Driving a parked row un-parks it (the ledger's parked -> live edge, which this verb alone writes); every dispatch also re-arms the report-or-die deadline so freshly-assigned work is never instantly overdue. The unpark transition is skipped when a verification was attempted and failed, mirroring clear_session's park posture. Only available on hosts whose driver provides a driver channel (currently 'headless' and 'tmux'); the degenerate 'operator' driver, and a headless/tmux process this build's memory no longer tracks (e.g. after a restart), both refuse with unsupported_on_host rather than silently doing nothing.
embedding_description: Send a work instruction, task brief, or follow-up prompt into a spawned fleet worker session over its live driver channel, un-parking it and refreshing its report-or-die deadline. Reports whether the drive was actually taken up as a turn, not merely sent. Distinct from clear_session/compact_session (hygiene, not work), spawn_session (no first turn), and peer_send (peer messaging, not stdin).

result_processor_customizations.result_description: lifecycle_state (the row's state after this call); unparked (true only when the row was parked and this dispatch drove the parked -> live transition); dispatched (the text reached the driver channel); submitted (true only on a POSITIVE observation that the driven text left the composer without ever being seen stranded there, null when this driver has no read-back surface -- never false, because a driver that looked and found it stranded raises drive_unverified instead); and drive_verification, naming which of those produced it: 'confirmed' or 'unsupported_on_driver'.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Read 'submitted', not success. A successful call means the command was DISPATCHED; only submitted=true means the drive was observed to leave the composer. When submitted is null, say plainly that this driver cannot confirm the effect and the drive is unverified -- never round that up to 'delivered' or 'done'. submitted=true is still not evidence the model acted on the text, only that it was taken up as a turn by this pane -- delivery to a surface is not delivery to a model. This verb previously returned a success shape for a drive that never landed, so do not reintroduce that reading in prose.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validates the text is non-empty, reads the managed_session ledger row, refuses on a terminal lifecycle_state, resolves the row's host driver, sends the text over its driver_channel(), then verifies the effect on drivers implementing the DriveVerifyingDriverChannel protocol (the tmux channel reads its pane with capture-pane -e, checking for the driven text stranded in bright-white styling before accepting an idle composer as a confirmed submit; the headless stream-json channel has no pane and reports unsupported_on_driver), re-arms report_by, then (parked rows only) writes the predicated parked -> live transition -- a fixed sequence, no retry loop anywhere in it.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: empty_text: nothing to dispatch -- the call was refused before any read. session_not_found: no managed_session row exists for the given agent_instance_id. lifecycle_state_conflict: the row is already terminated/retired -- terminal rows never receive driver-channel commands. unsupported_on_host: the row's host has no driver in this build, or its driver has no live driver channel for this host_ref (the degenerate 'operator' driver, or a headless process spawned before a restart wiped this build's in-memory tracking). driver_delivery_failed: the channel itself rejected the send. drive_unverified: the text WAS dispatched but the driver read the target back and never observed it leaving the composer -- either it is positively stranded there, or the verification deadline passed without a confirmed signal; either way the send happened, the effect did not. illegal_lifecycle_transition / stale_lifecycle_state: the un-park write lost a race with a concurrent sweep or verb -- the text WAS already sent; re-read session_status before retrying.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For drive_unverified, DO NOT re-send: the text is already sitting in that session's input buffer, and a blind retry deposits a second copy while still being unable to confirm itself. For unsupported_on_host, deliver the work another way for that session (e.g. peer_send to an operator-attended session) -- this verb has no fallback path, by design, to avoid a silent no-op. For stale_lifecycle_state, the dispatch itself already reached the worker; only the un-park bookkeeping lost the race -- check session_status before re-driving, or the worker receives the same brief twice.
